definitions.explanation: The overall size, shape, and structure of a person's body.

examples.japanese: {柔道|じゅうどう}の{選手|せんしゅ}はみんな{体格|たいかく}がいい。
examples.english: Judo athletes all have sturdy physiques.

examples.japanese: {体格|たいかく}の{差|さ}がありすぎて、{試合|しあい}にならなかった。
examples.english: The difference in build was so great that it wasn't even a match.

notes:
USAGE:
{体格|たいかく} refers to a person's overall physical build, focusing on size and frame rather than fitness or health. The phrase {体格|たいかく}がいい means "well-built" or "having a sturdy frame."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {体格|たいかく}がいい: well-built, having a good physique
- {体格|たいかく}{検査|けんさ}: physical examination
- {体格|たいかく}の{差|さ}: difference in build
- がっしりした{体格|たいかく}: a solid, muscular build

SIMILAR WORDS:
{体型|たいけい} focuses on body shape (slim, round, etc.), while {体格|たいかく} focuses on overall size and frame (large, sturdy, etc.).

WORD FORMATION:
{体|たい} (body) + {格|かく} (frame, structure).
